paper_title: Thinking Slow, Fast Scaling Inference Compute with Distilled Reasoners
caption: : Majority voting.
model_annotation: This plot illustrates majority voting accuracy as a function of the number of completions (k). The x-axis represents the number of completions (k) on a logarithmic base-2 scale, ranging from 2⁰ to 2⁸, with tick marks at each power of 2. The y-axis represents majority voting accuracy on a linear scale, ranging from approximately 0.25 to 0.6, with tick marks at 0.3, 0.4, 0.5, and 0.6. There are three lines in the plot. The first line, shown in dark blue with circle markers and a solid line style, begins at approximately 0.43 at k = 2⁰, rises gradually through the mid-range values, and reaches approximately 0.61 at k = 2⁸, with most of its increase occurring between k = 2⁰ and k = 2⁵ before leveling off. The second line, shown in green with triangle markers and a solid line style, starts at approximately 0.43 at k = 2⁰, increases steadily, and reaches approximately 0.61 at k = 2⁸, following a similar trajectory to the dark blue line though with a slightly more gradual rise in the early range and a steeper increase around k = 2² to k = 2⁴. The third line, shown in light green (or light blue-green) with triangle markers and a solid line style, begins at approximately 0.26 at k = 2⁰, increases slowly, and reaches approximately 0.45 at k = 2⁸, remaining consistently lower than the other two lines across the entire range of k values.
